newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European cash feeds sidelined by soaring futures.
newsitem.headline: European cash feeds sidelined by soaring futures.

text.p: The European meals and feeds trade remained sidelined on Tuesday as Chicago futures roared into life again at the start with weather fears sending positions soaring across the board.

"The market here is trading the absolute minimum possible," one trader said. "The buyers can still hang on for rain," he added, referring to the forecasts of hot weather in the U.S. Midwest, which sparked the price surge at Tuesday's opening.
Traders reported light business in Argentine soybeanmeal for afloat positions and some summer months. Higher offered prices for Brazilian material left the product untraded.
Elsewhere, the market for tapioca remained depressed, with the swine fever epidemic in the Netherlands taking its toll on demand for pigfeed, in which tapioca is a key ingredient.
Traders aaid they were expecting up to 700,000 tonnes less tapioca to be used by compounders in the year ahead as pigfeed production is predicted to be cut by some 2.5 million tonnes.
But the slack demand has not caused the build up of large stocks at the ports, as Thai shippers have pruned exports.
"Shippers in Thailand were quick to realise that keeping the tapioca there was cheaper than exporting it to a market that doesn't want it," one said. --Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
